item.title: Microsoft Patches Actively Exploited Outlook CVE-2026-124194 Amid 1,095 November Flaws
item.content:encoded:
Window: 10 Nov 23:00 → 11 Nov 03:00 UTC (4 hours)

Microsoft Patch Tuesday for November 2026 — Snort rules and prominent vulnerabilities — Optional

Microsoft’s November 2026 Patch Tuesday addresses 1,095 vulnerabilities, including 64 critical flaws and one Outlook spoofing issue reported as exploited in the wild. Organizations should prioritize updates for exposed Windows, Active Directory, Exchange, Office, Azure, and network-facing services, while deploying the accompanying Snort rule updates where applicable.

  • Microsoft’s November 2026 security update addresses 1,095 vulnerabilities, including 64 rated critical.
  • Microsoft stated that one disclosed vulnerability, CVE-2026-124194 in Microsoft Office Outlook, has been exploited in the wild.
  • Among the 64 critical vulnerabilities, 48 are remote code execution vulnerabilities.
  • Microsoft assessed several vulnerabilities as more likely to be exploited, including CVE-2026-113862 in Windows Network Address Translation, CVE-2026-118146 in Active Directory Domain Services, CVE-2026-118207 in Exchange Server, and CVE-2026-119952 in Windows Schannel.
  • Cisco Talos released Snort 2 and Snort 3 rules intended to detect attempts to exploit some of the disclosed vulnerabilities.

Technologies: operating-system, identity-provider, hypervisor, cloud-platform, message-queue, web-server, ci-cd, ids-ips

Products: windows, microsoft-office, microsoft-outlook, microsoft-exchange-server, active-directory-domain-services, windows-hyper-v, azure-managed-grafana, azure-openai, windows-message-queuing, internet-information-services, azure-devops-server, visual-studio-code, snort

Vendors: microsoft, cisco

Stop Blocking AI Calls. Start Redacting Them. — Optional

Netskope promotes entity-level redaction in its AI gateway and DLP tools to mask sensitive data in prompts and model responses without blocking AI workflows. The company argues this helps keep regulated data, customer information, and intellectual property out of LLMs while preserving auditability and compliance.

  • The article states that employees frequently paste confidential company data into generative AI prompts, including source code, regulated data, and intellectual property.
  • Netskope says its One DLP and Skylight AI Gateway inspect both requests sent to AI models and responses returned from them.
  • The described entity-redaction feature masks matched sensitive values, such as names, card numbers, identifiers, and health data, while allowing the AI request to continue.
  • Netskope says that keeping regulated data out of an AI model can reduce exposure risk and that forensic records can be stored in a customer-controlled destination.
  • The article argues that AI agents connected to business tools such as Slack, Teams, or Jira can expose sensitive information in model responses unless it is masked.

Technologies: dlp, api-gateway

Products: netskope-one-dlp, netskope-skylight-ai-gateway

Vendors: netskope

The Supply-Chain Risk Hiding in Your MCP Servers | Corelight — Optional

MCP servers introduce a supply-chain risk because they can connect AI agents to external tools and data sources with broad permissions, creating opportunities for compromised or malicious integrations to affect downstream systems. Organizations should inventory, vet, monitor, and tightly restrict MCP server capabilities before deployment.

  • The article focuses on supply-chain risk associated with MCP servers.
  • It presents MCP servers as a potential source of hidden risk.
  • The article is published by Corelight.

Vendors: corelight, anthropic

item.title: Railway and Qubole Cloud Breaches, Outlook Zero-Day Drive Digest
item.content:encoded:
Window: 10 Nov 19:00 → 10 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,235 flaws, Outlook zero-day — Must Read

Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes a record 1,235 vulnerabilities, including an actively exploited Outlook zero-day (CVE-2026-124194) that can leak NTLM authentication hashes when a victim opens a malicious message file. Organizations should prioritize deploying the updates, especially on systems running Outlook, Windows, Office, Edge, and server workloads.

  • Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday addresses 1,235 vulnerabilities, including 66 rated Critical.
  • The updates fix one actively exploited Outlook zero-day, CVE-2026-124194, a spoofing flaw that can expose NTLM authentication hashes.
  • Microsoft says an unauthenticated attacker can send a specially crafted message file that causes Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location if a user opens it.
  • The November updates include approximately 536 elevation-of-privilege, 296 remote-code-execution, 157 information-disclosure, 46 denial-of-service, 27 security-feature-bypass, and 22 spoofing vulnerabilities.
  • The reported total excludes 108 flaws fixed earlier in the month, including 82 Mariner and 25 Microsoft Edge vulnerabilities.

Technologies: operating-system, browser, database

Products: microsoft-outlook, windows-11, windows-10, microsoft-edge, microsoft-office, microsoft-exchange-server, microsoft-sql-server

Vendors: microsoft

Hackers exploit trusted AWS access to breach multiple cloud environments — Must Read

Attackers used compromised Qubole AWS IAM credentials to assume trusted cross-account roles at dozens of customer environments, steal secrets, and exfiltrate data from accessible S3 buckets. Organizations that trusted Qubole’s AWS account should review CloudTrail activity, revoke sessions, rotate credentials, and restrict or remove unused roles.

  • A threat actor used compromised IAM credentials for Qubole’s AWS account to access and steal data from customer AWS environments between October 14 and 26.
  • The attackers assumed cross-account roles in customer accounts that trusted Qubole, then searched cloud resources, retrieved stored secrets, and inspected Lambda environment variables.
  • The attackers used TruffleHog to validate discovered AWS keys, Microsoft Entra ID client secrets, and Okta client credentials before downloading accessible S3 bucket data.
  • Sentra confirmed dozens of victims and reported that millions of files were stolen from one customer, while the method used to compromise Qubole’s accounts remains unspecified.
  • Potentially affected administrators are advised to review CloudTrail logs from October 1 onward, investigate later secret and S3 access, rotate exposed credentials, revoke active role sessions, and restrict or remove unused integrations.

Technologies: iam, cloud-platform, secrets-manager, object-storage, identity-provider

Products: qubole, aws-identity-and-access-management, aws-security-token-service, aws-secrets-manager, aws-systems-manager-parameter-store, aws-lambda, amazon-s3, trufflehog, microsoft-entra-id, okta

Vendors: qubole, amazon-web-services, wiz, sentra, mandiant, microsoft, okta, truffle-security

Git Patches Flaw That Lets Malicious Repositories Execute Code During Recursive Clones — Should Read

Git patched CVE-2026-111760, a flaw that could let a malicious repository execute code during recursive clones by replacing a submodule’s .git file with a symlink to attacker-controlled hooks or configuration. Users should upgrade to Git 2.56.1 or the corresponding patched maintenance release and avoid recursively cloning untrusted repositories until updated.

  • Git fixed CVE-2026-111760 in Git 2.56.1 and corresponding maintenance releases after an integer truncation issue could enable code execution when a malicious repository is cloned recursively with submodules.
  • The flaw can cause an extremely long repository path to be written to disk under an attacker-controlled shorter name such as .git, allowing a submodule’s .git file to be replaced with a symbolic link to malicious hooks or configuration.
  • GitHub has applied the fixes to github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud, while GitHub Enterprise Server fixes are available in versions 3.19.15, 3.20.11, 3.21.9, and 3.22.4.
  • The Git releases also address five other flaws involving path traversal, stack-memory corruption, an out-of-bounds read, heap-memory corruption, and unsafe git fast-import features.
  • Until users install a fixed version, GitHub advises cloning only from trusted servers and avoiding recursive clones, untrusted merges or tags, binary patches, and fast-import streams from untrusted sources.

Technologies: source-control, cloud-platform, ci-cd

Products: git, github-enterprise-server, github-enterprise-cloud, github-desktop, github-copilot, github-codespaces, github-actions, git-for-windows, gitlab

Vendors: git-project, github, gitlab, git-for-windows

Railway breach leads to $740,000 in fraudulent AI charges — Should Read

Railway says attackers exploited two infrastructure flaws, accessed decrypted environment variables for up to 100,000 workspaces, and used stolen AI credentials to incur about $740,000 in fraudulent charges. Customers should rotate secrets, while Railway says it has removed the attackers, remediated the flaws, and will cover unreimbursed charges.

  • Railway says attackers exploited an unknown flaw in its build infrastructure on October 20 to escape file-system isolation, obtain an internal credential, and access build histories and its internal source code.
  • The attackers then exploited an improperly configured trust relationship to obtain credentials used to decrypt customer environment variables, potentially affecting up to 1.85% of Railway workspaces, or about 100,000.
  • Railway says the stolen credentials were used to generate approximately $740,000 in unauthorized AI usage, and it will cover charges that AI providers do not refund.
  • The incident also exposed linked-account tokens for 1,852 users, including GitHub OAuth tokens and AI agent keys; Railway reset the tokens and notified affected users.
  • Railway says it removed the attackers from its systems on October 21, remediated the exploited flaws, and found no evidence that customer Git repositories or databases were accessed.

Technologies: cloud-platform, ci-cd, iam, secrets-manager

Products: railway, github-oauth

Vendors: railway, github

Japanese furniture giant Nitori says hackers stole 37.6M customer records — Should Read

Japanese furniture retailer Nitori says unauthorized access to its systems may have exposed up to 37.62 million customer records, including contact details and order information. Passwords and credit-card data were not affected, but customers are being warned about phishing and scams.

  • Nitori said unauthorized access to a company-managed system was confirmed on November 6, 2026, and its investigation indicates the attacker may have had access since mid-October.
  • The company said up to 37.62 million personal-information records may have been leaked externally.
  • Affected data may include customer and corporate member contact details, dates of birth, gender, company information, and online-order information from Nitori Net and official marketplace shops.
  • Nitori said registered-member passwords and credit-card information were not exposed.
  • The company blocked the unauthorized access, addressed system weaknesses, informed relevant Japanese authorities, and warned customers to be alert for phishing and scam attempts.

Products: nitori-net

SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users — Should Read

An attacker exploited an SGLang remote-code-execution flaw to breach NEAR AI infrastructure, exposing data from 18 AI agents and account details for about 100 users, with possible access to requests processed on an affected inference server. NEAR AI patched the issue, rotated credentials and tokens, revoked exposed API keys, and notified confirmed affected users.

  • An attacker exploited a remote-code-execution flaw in the SGLang inference engine to run code on a NEAR AI inference server.
  • The attacker may have viewed requests processed by the affected server, including requests in confidential mode, because SGLang ran inside the protected processing environment.
  • The attacker accessed an internal system behind NEAR AI’s deprecated Private Chat product and downloaded account details for about 100 users, including names and email addresses.
  • The attacker accessed 18 AI agents on an older NEAR AI Agents deployment and took chat histories, settings, and logs; logs exposed two customers’ NEAR AI Cloud API keys.
  • NEAR AI says it patched the SGLang flaw on its inference servers, revoked active sessions and administrator credentials, replaced agent tokens, rotated remaining credentials, and notified confirmed affected users.

Technologies: cloud-platform, browser

Products: sglang, private-chat, near-ai-agents, near-ai-cloud, leo, glm-5-3-flash

Vendors: near-ai, sglang-project, brave

Microsoft releases Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update — Should Read

Microsoft released the Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update for ESU and Enterprise LTSC users, bringing systems to build 19045.7846 and including November 2026 security fixes. It also resolves remaining USB Audio Class 1.0 problems, printer and Remote Desktop issues, and adds stricter PowerShell script-signing encoding validation.

  • Microsoft released the Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update, which includes November 2026 Patch Tuesday security fixes and bug fixes.
  • The update is available through Windows Update for Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC users and users enrolled in the Extended Security Updates program.
  • After installation, Windows 10 reaches build 19045.7846 and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 reaches build 19044.7846.
  • KB5131096 fixes an Active Directory printer-addition error, Remote Desktop policy and shadow-connection issues, and remaining USB Audio Class 1.0 problems caused by September 2026 security updates.
  • The update adds stricter encoding validation for PowerShell script signing, which can cause scripts with invalid UTF-8 encoding to fail signature validation.

Technologies: operating-system, iam, remote-access

Products: windows-10, windows-10-enterprise-ltsc-2021, windows-update, microsoft-intune, remote-desktop, windows-powershell

Vendors: microsoft

US Army member arrested in UK over allegations of spying for Russia — May Read

A 41-year-old U.S. Army soldier was arrested in Gloucestershire, UK, on suspicion of spying for Russia under the UK National Security Act. British counterterrorism police are investigating alongside U.S. authorities, including the FBI and U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command.

  • A 41-year-old U.S. Army soldier was arrested near Gloucester, UK, on suspicion of spying for Russia.
  • UK counterterrorism police said they worked closely with U.S. authorities, including the FBI and U.S. military, during the investigation.
  • The arrest was made under provisions of the UK National Security Act concerning espionage, and police searched two locations in Gloucestershire.
  • The head of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command said the arrested senior soldier had been entrusted with sensitive information.
  • GCHQ Director Anne Keast-Butler said Russia has been relentlessly targeting critical infrastructure, democratic processes, supply chains, and public trust.

item.title: Fireworks AI Breach, SAP CVE-2026-89103, and AhsayCBS Exploitation Lead Threats
item.content:encoded:
Window: 10 Nov 15:00 → 10 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-89103) SAP Gateway Authentication Bypass via Default Access Control List — Must Read

SAP Gateway has a critical pre-authentication authentication-bypass flaw, CVE-2026-89103, that can let network-accessible attackers be treated as trusted internal application servers. Organizations should urgently apply SAP Security Note 3798345 and restrict external access to gateway ports TCP/33NN and TCP/48NN.

  • CVE-2026-89103 is a critical SAP Gateway access-control flaw with a CVSS v3.1 score of 10.0 that can allow a network-accessible attacker to be treated as an internal application server before authentication.
  • Affected systems include SAP NetWeaver application servers and other SAP systems using affected kernel releases when their gateway ports are reachable, typically TCP/33NN and TCP/48NN.
  • SAP released a kernel-update correction in Security Note 3798345 during its November 2026 Security Patch Day, and published analysis indicates older kernels may require the gw/acl_mode_proxy setting after patching.
  • Until patching is confirmed, the article recommends blocking internet access to gateway ports, replacing default gateway rules with explicit secinfo and reginfo entries, and monitoring for unexpected external program registrations.
  • CyCognito observed potentially exposed SAP NetWeaver assets across multiple sectors, led by Information Technology and Communication Services.

Products: sap-gateway, sap-netweaver

Vendors: sap, cycognito

Attackers Exploit AhsayCBS Flaws to Deploy Sandbox-Evading Python Backdoor — Should Read

Attackers exploited two now-patched AhsayCBS zero-day flaws to compromise backup servers, deploy JSP web shells, XMRig miners, tunneling tools, and a host-locked Python backdoor designed to evade sandbox analysis. The intrusion also targeted backup infrastructure credentials, including a Veeam database query intended to decrypt stored credentials.

  • Huntress observed attackers exploiting CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 in AhsayCBS to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands before Ahsay Backup released patches in mid-October 2026.
  • The attackers deployed five families of JSP web shells, including AhsayCBS.jsp, which hides encrypted payloads in PNG pixel data and executes them from memory.
  • The intrusion deployed two XMRig cryptocurrency miners, including one masquerading as Microsoft Edge and another configured to restart every minute through a SYSTEM scheduled task.
  • A Python backdoor named main.py checks a hash derived from the host MachineGuid before running an in-memory DLL that contacts creepexplosiondarknight[.]com, helping prevent execution in sandboxes or on analysts' machines.
  • On a related Veeam server, Huntress observed a PowerShell command consistent with NetExec's Veeam credential-theft module querying the VeeamBackup PostgreSQL database and decrypting stored credentials with DPAPI.

Technologies: backup, antivirus, remote-access

Products: ahsaycbs, microsoft-defender, veeam-backup, anydesk, atera, splashtop

Vendors: ahsay-backup, microsoft, veeam, anydesk, atera, splashtop

Blind Eagle Uses Fake Court Notices to Deliver Remote Access Trojan Across Latin America — Should Read

Blind Eagle is running a large phishing campaign across Latin America using fake court and government notices to deliver an AsyncRAT/DCRat-derived remote-access trojan. The chain uses weaponized SVG files, HTML smuggling, AMSI/ETW bypasses, and startup persistence, with Colombia a key target.

  • Blind Eagle, also known as APT-C-36, used fake judicial and administrative notices in Spanish and Portuguese to target organizations in Latin America with a remote-access trojan.
  • The phishing chain included a weaponized SVG file impersonating Colombia’s Fiscalía General de la Nación, which created a ZIP archive locally in the recipient’s browser.
  • A JavaScript dropper collected system information, then launched a script that bypassed Windows security monitoring features and displayed a fake criminal-citation page.
  • The final payload was an AsyncRAT fork with DCRat lineage that was decoded and launched in memory using PowerShell.
  • Zenox observed nearly 3,300 malicious emails in a targeted phishing wave between late October and early November 2026, although it could not confirm successful compromises.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access

Products: windows, powershell, asyncrat, dcrat

Vendors: microsoft, zenox

Fireworks AI Breach Widens to Expose Customer Billing Data and Incomplete Model Weights — Should Read

Fireworks AI expanded its breach disclosure after attackers accessed customer billing data, resource metadata, secrets, datasets, and incomplete model weights through compromised internal and third-party cloud access. The incident also affected fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces, potentially exposing Notion AI Insights chat transcripts.

  • Fireworks AI said its investigation found that attackers accessed account and billing information, secrets, datasets, and incomplete model weights for a limited set of customer accounts.
  • The company said attackers reached its development environment through an unnamed third-party cloud provider hosting Fireworks R&D machines and then ran an unauthorized workload.
  • The exposed billing information may include billing and shipping addresses, invoice and payment history, account balances, and credit usage, while Fireworks AI said it does not store payment card numbers.
  • Fireworks AI linked the activity to a financially motivated cybercriminal group seeking to sell stolen access to large language models through illicit routing gateways.
  • Notion said the incident affected fewer than 1% of its workspaces and may have included Notion AI Insights chat transcripts, prompting it to disable the Insights feature.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: fireworks-ai-platform, notion-ai, insights

Vendors: fireworks-ai, notion, google

Cybercriminals are increasingly infecting regular people with spyware — May Read

iVerify reports that criminal spyware infections on consumer iPhones are rising, with leaked Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits enabling large-scale web-based compromises for credential and cryptocurrency theft. The shift means sophisticated mobile surveillance capabilities once largely limited to nation-state operations are increasingly threatening ordinary users and employees.

  • iVerify reported 1.07 spyware infections per 1,000 consumer device scans, compared with 0.7 per 1,000 enterprise scans.
  • About 75% of iVerify’s detections involved criminal actors using the Coruna or DarkSword iOS exploit kits, while 25% involved mercenary spyware such as Pegasus.
  • DarkSword can infect a device through a compromised website without the visitor clicking a link, while Coruna uses web-based attacks involving WebKit and kernel flaws.
  • The report said infected DarkSword and Coruna device owners did not receive Apple threat notifications, despite the tools’ ability to access messages, photos, emails, microphones, and cameras.
  • iVerify said the findings show mobile spyware has expanded from a tool primarily associated with nation-state targeting to a broad cybercrime risk affecting ordinary users and employees.

Technologies: mobile-os, browser

Products: ios, webkit, coruna, darksword, pegasus

Vendors: apple, iverify, google, l3harris

Sage: AI for Assumed-Breach Operations, Built Into Mythic — Optional

SpecterOps has released Sage, an open-source AI assistant embedded in Mythic v4 that helps operators plan and execute assumed-breach operations across Mythic agents while requiring approval for each action in supervised mode. Sage uses BloodHound and a proof-backed engagement ledger to preserve operational context, with autonomous operation restricted to research labs.

  • SpecterOps released Sage as an open-source AI assistant that runs inside Mythic v4 and helps operators translate objectives into proposed actions across available Mythic agents.
  • Sage offers conversation, supervised, and autonomous modes; supervised mode requires approval for every guarded action, while autonomous mode is described as an experimental research capability for lab environments.
  • Sage stores operational context in BloodHound and an Engagement State Ledger, where claimed gains are recorded as achieved only when supported by Mythic, credential, callback, task, file, or BloodHound evidence.
  • Sage can learn command schemas from installed Mythic payload types, validate proposed arguments before tasking, and use built-in capabilities that convert selected actions into concrete Mythic commands.
  • The project is beta software validated primarily with Mythic v4, LiteLLM, and the Apollo payload, with other providers and Mythic agents supported but not yet fully validated.

Products: sage, mythic, bloodhound, apollo, merlin, langgraph, langchain, litellm, arize-phoenix, nemesis, rubeus, certify, goad

Vendors: specterops, mythicagents, anthropic, openai, amazon-web-services, ollama, arize

item.title: Turla Exchange Espionage and CopperDragon Sparrow Campaigns Lead Threat Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 10 Nov 11:00 → 10 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Not All That Glitters Is Gold: Tracking CopperDragon’s Sparrow Framework Around the Globe — Should Read

Check Point Research links three espionage clusters targeting telecoms, governments, critical infrastructure, and research organizations across Latin America, Asia, and Europe to CopperDragon, a suspected supplier of the Sparrow malware framework to China-nexus actors. The campaigns use distinct access methods and implants—including watering holes, compromised Linux servers, SquadC, SparrowDoor/SparrowShell, CopperDoor, and CopperDNS—to enable credential theft, persistence, lateral movement, and covert command-and-control.

  • Check Point Research identified three operational clusters—SilentDelivery, OceanGate, and DarkWire—linked through shared infrastructure features and malware-code similarities in the Sparrow framework.
  • SilentDelivery used selective compromised-website campaigns in Europe and Asia to display fake Chrome certificate warnings and deliver SquadC or SparrowDoor through fraudulent certificate-repair installers.
  • OceanGate targeted government organizations and critical infrastructure primarily in Asia, initially compromising internet-facing Linux systems before moving into Windows environments for credential theft, lateral movement, and data collection.
  • DarkWire targeted telecommunications providers and government organizations, initially concentrated in Latin America, using CopperDoor and the DNS-tunneling CopperDNS backdoors.
  • Check Point tracks CopperDragon as a possible developer and supplier of the cross-platform Sparrow framework used by several China-nexus threat actors, including FamousSparrow, Earth Estries, TropicTrooper, and UAT-9244.

Technologies: operating-system, browser, object-storage, vpn

Products: windows, google-chrome, amazon-s3, softether-vpn, windivert, openssh

Vendors: microsoft, google, amazon-web-services, softether

Russian hackers compromised government email servers to steal NATO, EU correspondence — Should Read

ESET says Russia-linked Turla hackers compromised government Microsoft Exchange servers in Romania and Kazakhstan using a new stealthy toolkit called Cereal to intercept sensitive emails, including NATO and EU correspondence. The group used the victims’ own Exchange infrastructure as a command hub, making the espionage campaign harder to detect and disrupt.

  • ESET attributed a campaign targeting government Microsoft Exchange servers in Romania and Kazakhstan to Turla, a Russian state-linked espionage group associated with the FSB.
  • The attackers used a previously unknown toolkit called Cereal, including a component named CerealBox, to monitor email traffic and capture selected messages.
  • In Romania, the malware was configured to collect emails exchanged with NATO and European Union institutions.
  • The attackers used compromised Exchange servers themselves to issue commands and manage the operation, reducing reliance on external infrastructure.
  • ESET said it could not determine how the attackers initially accessed the government servers or how much information they obtained.

Products: microsoft-exchange-server

Vendors: eset, microsoft

Binance Warns of iOS Sandbox Escape That Could Expose Crypto Wallet Keys, No Fix Confirmed — Should Read

Binance warned that the publicly released worse_query iOS sandbox escape may let malicious sideloaded apps access other apps’ data, potentially exposing crypto wallet seed phrases, private keys, and credentials on iOS 26 and 27. Apple’s latest updates do not confirm a fix, so users should remove untrusted apps and move funds to a new wallet if compromise is suspected.

  • A researcher known as forcequit published worse_query, an iOS sandbox escape that can let an app access data containers belonging to other apps on iPhones running iOS 26 and 27.
  • Binance warned that exposed app data could include cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials, though no attacks or theft involving worse_query have been reported.
  • The WQ Files file manager uses worse_query to read, edit, delete, and clear other apps’ data without a jailbreak or kernel exploit, and it is installed through sideloading tools such as AltStore and SideStore.
  • Apple’s iOS 27.2.1 and iOS 26.7.3 security notes do not mention worse_query or an iOS sandbox fix.
  • Binance advised users to remove apps from untrusted sources, update iOS and apps, and move funds to a new wallet created on a clean device if they suspect compromise.

Technologies: mobile-os

Products: ios-26, ios-27, worse-query, wq-files, erosion, altstore, sidestore

Vendors: apple, binance, forcequitos, wq-files, erosion, altstore, sidestore

Palantir exec nominated to lead CISA; lame-duck Senate vote is uncertain — May Read

President Trump nominated Palantir CIO Michael LoSapio to lead CISA, but a Senate vote during the crowded lame-duck session is uncertain. If not confirmed before adjournment, the nomination must be resubmitted to an incoming Democratic-majority Senate, where Palantir ties may draw greater scrutiny.

  • President Donald Trump nominated Palantir Chief Information Officer Michael LoSapio to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
  • CISA has lacked a Senate-confirmed leader since Trump returned to office, with Nick Andersen serving as acting leader since February after previous nominee Sean Plankey withdrew.
  • During the second Trump administration, CISA lost more than 1,000 personnel—about one-third of its workforce—and its budget was reduced by billions of dollars.
  • It is unclear whether the Senate will consider LoSapio's nomination during the crowded lame-duck session; if it does not, Trump would need to renominate him next year.
  • LoSapio could face greater scrutiny in an incoming Democratic-majority Senate because of his role at Palantir, a software and artificial intelligence company with ties to the Trump administration.

Vendors: palantir

Beyond the Alert: The Case for Rich Network Data — Optional

Corelight argues that effective network incident response depends on rich, searchable network evidence—not just alerts—so analysts and AI can trace activity, validate findings, and understand an attack’s full scope. The sponsored article urges buyers to evaluate NDR tools by how deeply their data supports investigation beyond a guided demo.

  • The article argues that preventing every security incident is not possible, so teams need to find and disrupt activity that has entered their networks.
  • An alert may identify a suspicious connection, but detailed network data is needed to trace activity before, after, and across systems and determine an incident’s scope.
  • Rich network data can include transaction details, packet content, extracted files, searchable history, and context that allows analysts to follow connections over time.
  • AI tools can process large amounts of security data and help investigate unfamiliar services, processes, and log formats, but their outputs still need to be checked against evidence.
  • The article recommends evaluating network security products by investigating an alert beyond a guided demonstration to see whether the available data supports unanticipated questions and deeper analysis.

Technologies: network-monitoring

Products: corelight-ndr

Vendors: corelight

item.title: Active Barracuda and Chrome Exploits, Turla Exchange Espionage, and SAP CVSS 10s
item.content:encoded:
Window: 10 Nov 07:00 → 10 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers now exploit critical Barracuda ESG flaws to gain root access — Must Read

Barracuda warns that attackers are actively exploiting two recently patched flaws in its appliances, which can be chained to bypass authorization and execute commands as root. Customers should apply patches immediately and restrict administrative-interface access to trusted networks.

  • Barracuda warned that attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560, two recently patched flaws affecting its Email Security Gateway and other products.
  • CVE-2026-116606 is an authentication weakness in Barracuda Email Security Gateway that can allow modification of an appliance’s global configuration, while CVE-2026-111560 permits unauthenticated operating-system command injection with root privileges.
  • Barracuda said the vulnerabilities can be combined to bypass authorization controls and obtain root access, but exploitation requires access to an affected device’s administrative interface.
  • The company identified exploitation affecting a small number of organizations and urged customers to manually install the relevant patch if it was not automatically applied.
  • Affected products include Barracuda Email Security Gateway, Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall, and Web Security Gateway.

Technologies: email-security, load-balancer, waf, proxy

Products: barracuda-email-security-gateway, barracuda-load-balancer-adc, barracuda-message-archiver, barracuda-waf-control-center, barracuda-web-application-firewall, barracuda-web-security-gateway

Vendors: barracuda-networks, mandiant

Google patches eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in attacks this year — Must Read

Google released emergency Chrome updates to fix CVE-2026-125350, a high-severity use-after-free flaw in the browser's XML component that is already being exploited in the wild. Users should update Chrome to version 157.0.8103.50/.51 as soon as possible.

  • Google released emergency Chrome security updates for CVE-2026-125350, a high-severity use-after-free flaw in Chrome's XML component that it says is being exploited in the wild.
  • The flaw can enable memory corruption when Chrome later accesses memory that has already been freed, potentially allowing attackers to manipulate memory layout and execute malicious code.
  • Google did not disclose details about the observed attacks and said vulnerability details may remain restricted until most users have received the fix.
  • The update is rolling out through Chrome's Stable Desktop channel for Windows, macOS version 157.0.8103.50/.51, and Linux version 157.0.8103.50.
  • CVE-2026-125350 is the eighth Chrome zero-day vulnerability Google has patched this year after evidence of active exploitation.

Technologies: browser

Products: google-chrome, chromium

Vendors: google, chromium-project

SAP Patches Four CVSS 10.0 Flaws, Including Two Enabling Remote Code Execution — Must Read

SAP released urgent patches for four unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws affecting NetWeaver and Web Dispatcher, including two remote-code-execution bugs, a SAML login bypass, and SAP Gateway server impersonation. Organizations should prioritize patching exposed systems and restrict direct access to ICM and Gateway ports.

  • SAP released fixes for four unauthenticated vulnerabilities rated CVSS 10.0 in its November Security Patch Day bulletin.
  • CVE-2026-76964 in SAP NetWeaver Internet Communication Manager and CVE-2026-89126 in SAP Web Dispatcher can allow remote code execution through crafted network traffic that corrupts memory.
  • CVE-2026-120017 can allow an attacker to sign in as any user, including privileged users, on affected SAML single-sign-on configurations.
  • CVE-2026-89103 can allow an external attacker to impersonate an SAP application server and take unauthorized actions through SAP Gateway.
  • SAP and RedRays recommend prioritizing the patches, updating kernels and Web Dispatchers together, and restricting direct network access to Gateway and Internet Communication Manager ports.

Technologies: web-server, proxy, load-balancer, iam, api-gateway

Products: sap-netweaver-as-abap, sap-web-dispatcher, sap-gateway, sap-internet-communication-manager, sap-hana-xs-classic, sap-hana-xs-advanced

Vendors: sap

France Blames Iran for Sabotage Attack on Refrigeration Controllers at About 700 Retail Sites — Must Read

France has attributed an October sabotage campaign against internet-exposed refrigeration controllers at roughly 700 retail sites to Iran’s IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh unit, causing major food losses and about 20 fires. Authorities urge operators to remove affected Danfoss, Dixell, and Copeland systems from public internet access and restore remote access only through secured networks.

  • France attributed an October sabotage campaign targeting refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail and food-sector sites to Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
  • Attackers remotely accessed Danfoss and Dixell controllers, set unlimited high-temperature defrost cycles, and disabled temperature-probe safety alerts, causing food losses and about 20 fires.
  • Most affected organizations were large French retailers including Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché, while smaller butcher shops, a slaughterhouse, and cooperative food plants were also hit.
  • French authorities opened a judicial investigation, plan to summon Iran’s ambassador, and will seek additional European sanctions against those involved.
  • CERT-FR advised operators to remove affected controllers from public internet access, review configurations, update supported devices, change default passwords, and use a secure VPN or protected network for remote access.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device

Products: danfoss-ak-sm, danfoss-ak-sc, copeland-xweb, dixell-xweb

Vendors: danfoss, dixell, copeland, schneider-electric

Turla hackers use new Cereal malware to spy on govt Exchange servers — Should Read

Russia-linked Turla used its new Cereal malware framework to covertly spy on Microsoft Exchange email servers at government organizations in Kazakhstan and Romania. The toolset intercepts selected emails and executes commands in memory while avoiding separate command-and-control infrastructure.

  • ESET found Turla's Cereal toolset on Microsoft Exchange servers at a government organization in Kazakhstan in late 2025 and at a Romanian government agency compromised on December 23, 2025.
  • Turla used the CerealBox component to enter Exchange's EdgeTransport.exe process and take over existing email-processing handlers without registering a new handler or interrupting mail delivery.
  • The malware selectively collected emails matching specified sender, recipient, and subject criteria, particularly messages with DOC, DOCX, or PDF attachments.
  • CerealNeuron accepted encrypted requests disguised as legitimate Exchange service paths, ran attacker-provided programs in memory, and returned encrypted results.
  • ESET observed no external command-and-control infrastructure in the campaign, with the compromised Exchange server acting as the attackers' only control point.

Technologies: email-security

Products: microsoft-exchange-server

Vendors: microsoft, eset

Apple Patches iMessage Group Chat Privacy Flaws and Bluetooth Pairing Vulnerabilities — Should Read

Apple released security updates fixing iMessage flaws that could expose group-chat messages or allow unauthorized joining, along with an actively exploited Brotli memory-corruption bug and Bluetooth pairing vulnerabilities. Users should install the available updates promptly.

  • Apple released updates that fix iMessage issues that could allow a remote attacker to join a group chat and receive its messages, or allow a newly added member to access messages sent before joining.
  • The iMessage issues are tracked as CVE-2026-113961, an authorization issue addressed through improved validation, and CVE-2026-113960.
  • The same updates fix CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in Google’s Brotli decoder that could allow malicious input to corrupt memory and was added to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 27.
  • Apple’s iOS 18.7.12 and watchOS 26.6.1 notes list other security fixes but do not list the iMessage or Brotli fixes.
  • All nine updates address Bluetooth and AirPlay issues, including flaws that could allow a malicious nearby Bluetooth device to pair without user interaction or bypass pairing-code attempt limits.

Technologies: mobile-os

Products: imessage, ios, ipados, watchos, airplay, google-brotli

Vendors: apple, google, brotli

Fireworks AI discloses new breach after cloud provider hack — Should Read

Fireworks AI disclosed a second October breach in which attackers leveraged a compromised third-party cloud provider to access development machines and obtain customer metadata, billing information, and some incomplete model weights and datasets. The company says it contained the incident, rotated credentials, and found no further unauthorized access after October 25.

  • Fireworks AI disclosed that attackers accessed its development machines on October 24 after a third-party cloud provider hosting its research-and-development machines suffered a security incident on October 23.
  • The unauthorized workload run on Fireworks development machines exposed customer resource metadata, billing information, and incomplete model weights and datasets for some customers.
  • Fireworks said payment-card numbers were not exposed because the company does not store them.
  • Fireworks detected the activity on October 24 and said it had found no further evidence of successful unauthorized access to its customer platform as of October 25.
  • The company revoked and replaced credentials and service accounts, restricted unauthorized network paths, isolated affected systems, and is working with Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 on the investigation and security improvements.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Vendors: fireworks-ai, palo-alto-networks

Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 Beats GPT-6 Cyber in Multi-Stage Cyberattack Benchmark — Should Read

Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, claiming stronger coding and cybersecurity capabilities, with Fable 5.2 achieving a 76.3% success rate on Irregular’s multi-stage CyScenarioBench—above GPT-6 Cyber’s 61%. Anthropic also expanded Claude Security with continuous code scanning and fix tracking.

  • Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, reporting improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision.
  • On Irregular’s CyScenarioBench, Claude Fable 5.2 completed 76.3% of challenges, compared with 61.7% for Fable 5.1 and 61% for OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber.
  • Anthropic said Fable 5.2 scored 89.6% on its CVE Rediscovery benchmark, which tests whether a model can rediscover known software flaws using affected source code.
  • Anthropic described Claude Mythos 5.2 as its most capable model for cybersecurity engineering and said its cyber capabilities are available through the Cyber Verification Program.
  • Anthropic updated Claude Security with continuous code scanning and automatic fix tracking to help teams identify and address weaknesses as code changes.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: claude-fable-5-2, claude-mythos-5-2, claude-security, cyscenariobench, gpt-6-cyber, gemini-4-argon, amazon-web-services, google-cloud, microsoft-azure

Vendors: anthropic, irregular, openai, google, amazon-web-services, microsoft

IT threat evolution in Q3 2026. Non-mobile statistics — Optional

Kaspersky’s Q3 2026 telemetry recorded more than 311 million web-based attacks, 23.7 million malicious or unwanted local objects, and ransomware targeting 81,556 users, with Qilin the most prolific extortion group by leak-site victims. The report also highlights active exploitation of enterprise product flaws, growing macOS supply-chain and stealer activity, and shifting IoT botnet attack patterns.

  • In Q3 2026, Kaspersky products blocked 311,083,655 attacks from online resources and Web Anti-Virus detected 46,936,926 unique URLs.
  • Kaspersky protected 81,556 unique users from ransomware attacks in Q3 2026 and detected 4,470 new ransomware variants across three new ransomware families.
  • Qilin accounted for 15.39% of victims published on ransomware groups’ data leak sites during the reporting period, making it the most prolific group in the review.
  • Kaspersky detected miner attacks affecting 217,024 unique users worldwide and identified 2,197 new miner variants in Q3 2026.
  • Kaspersky File Anti-Virus recorded 23,733,652 malicious and potentially unwanted objects, while 10.88% of users’ computers worldwide encountered a local malware threat at least once during the quarter.

Technologies: antivirus, firewall, remote-access, operating-system, hypervisor, ci-cd, package-registry, iot-device

Products: sma1000, sharepoint-server, windows, vcenter, firebox, teamcity, macos, npm, pypi, cargo

Vendors: kaspersky, palo-alto-networks, sonicwall, microsoft, vmware, watchguard, jetbrains, apple

IT threat evolution in Q3 2026. Mobile statistics — Optional

Kaspersky recorded 1.67 million blocked mobile threats in Q3 2026, with banking Trojans—especially Mamont—and packaged droppers driving much of the malicious-app activity. The quarter also saw AI-enabled Android fraud tools and iOS spyware campaigns exploiting DarkSword through compromised packages and fake App Store apps.

  • Kaspersky blocked more than 1.66 million attacks involving mobile malware, adware, or unwanted software in Q3 2026, down from 1,996,823 in Q2.
  • Trojan-Banker threats accounted for 31.63% of detected malicious mobile apps, and Kaspersky detected 119,688 mobile banking Trojan installation packages.
  • Kaspersky identified Android apps that used on-device AI models to interpret fraud commands or search screenshots and gallery images for banking information, including CVV codes.
  • The Mamont banking Trojan remained the most active banking threat in attacks, while Creduz accounted for the largest share of detected banking-Trojan packages.
  • iOS campaigns used the DarkSword exploit chain through infected Packagist packages and a fake App Store crypto wallet tracker, with spyware designed to steal data including keychain contents, Wi-Fi passwords, SMS messages, photos, and crypto wallet recovery phrases.

Technologies: mobile-os, package-registry

Products: android, ios, google-play, google-play-protect, app-store, packagist

Vendors: kaspersky, google, apple, packagist

item.title: CISA Flags Active Exploitation of OpenSSH SSHole and Three Enterprise Flaws
item.content:encoded:
Window: 10 Nov 03:00 → 10 Nov 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA Warns of Active Exploitation of OpenSSH, GPUStack, FreeSWITCH, and IBM Flaws — Must Read

CISA added critical flaws in OpenSSH, GPUStack, FreeSWITCH, and IBM Aspera Faspex to its KEV catalog after evidence of active exploitation. Organizations should urgently apply available patches, particularly for OpenSSH’s SSHole authentication-bypass flaw, which attackers are using for reconnaissance, persistence, botnet activity, and cryptomining.

  • CISA added four actively exploited vulnerabilities affecting IBM Aspera Faspex, SignalWire FreeSWITCH, OpenBSD OpenSSH, and GPUStack to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
  • The OpenSSH flaw, CVE-2026-123158 or SSHole, is an authentication-bypass issue on Linux that was fixed in November 2026 and has faced exploitation attempts since November 6, 2026.
  • GreyNoise reported confirmed post-exploitation activity from six source IP addresses involving reconnaissance, cloud metadata queries, attempts to read password hashes and root SSH keys, and modification of SSH authorized_keys files.
  • Attackers were observed deploying TAC Agent, a Python-based remote-control tool that can execute shell commands, perform system reconnaissance, enumerate directories, transfer files, and update itself.
  • Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies are recommended to apply fixes for the four vulnerabilities by November 12, 2026.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: ibm-aspera-faspex, freeswitch, openssh, gpustack

Vendors: ibm, signalwire, openbsd, gpustack

item.title: N-able N-central Zero-Days Prompt Shutdown as Refrigeration Attacks Trigger US Warning
item.content:encoded:
Window: 09 Nov 19:00 → 09 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

N-able takes cloud platform offline after 30+ "zero-days" published — Should Read

N-able took its hosted N-central platform offline worldwide and told on-premises customers to shut down servers after a researcher publicly released more than 30 alleged zero-days, including an unauthenticated XXE chain that can yield administrator access and remote code execution. N-able is developing a hotfix and says it has found no evidence of active exploitation so far.

  • Security researcher Sean Bales publicly disclosed more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities in N-able N-central and released proof-of-concept exploits in the Able2Shell GitHub repository.
  • The disclosed issues include a reported unauthenticated XML external entity flaw that can be chained to reset an account password, create a Default Administrator account, and execute commands on an N-central server as the nable user.
  • N-able took hosted N-central environments offline across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific and advised customers with on-premises N-central servers to take them offline temporarily.
  • N-able said it is developing and validating a hotfix, and that it has found no evidence of active exploitation or unauthorized data access.
  • Bales said he released the N-central findings without prior notice because N-able allegedly had not patched or responded to reports of unrelated flaws in another product that he submitted months earlier.

Technologies: network-monitoring, remote-access

Products: n-central, n-central-appliance

Vendors: n-able

U.S. urges critical infrastructure orgs to secure refrigeration systems ASAP after EU supermarket and blood bank attacks — Should Read

U.S. agencies are urging critical-infrastructure operators to immediately harden internet-exposed industrial refrigeration and cold-chain systems after attacks in Europe spoiled food and threatened blood supplies through remote temperature manipulation.

  • U.S. agencies warned critical infrastructure organizations to secure industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems following cyberattacks on French blood banks and European supermarkets.
  • Attackers are remotely targeting commercial refrigeration controllers by exploiting unpatched flaws, misconfigurations, and weak or hard-coded passwords, then manipulating temperatures to spoil products.
  • CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA, and the Department of Transportation recommend changing default passwords, patching critical flaws, replacing end-of-life devices, identifying internet-accessible systems, isolating operational systems, limiting remote access, and maintaining offsite backups.
  • French authorities have investigated attacks since mid-October involving compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and Copeland and Dixell XWEB controllers.
  • The attacks on French grocery stores caused food to spoil and triggered fires, while temperature manipulation can also affect essential products such as blood and medicines.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device

Products: danfoss-ak-sm, danfoss-ak-sc, copeland-refrigeration-controllers, dixell-xweb, tenable-one

Vendors: danfoss, copeland, dixell, tenable

SEGA newsletter data breach exposes 2.2 million email addresses — Should Read

SEGA says a breach at newsletter provider ARARA exposed 2.2 million subscriber email addresses, with another 92,300 records containing still-undetermined additional data. The incident is part of a wider ARARA compromise affecting 77 million email addresses across nearly 380 clients, though SEGA reports no confirmed misuse and says its separate SEGA Account system was unaffected.

  • SEGA disclosed that a breach at its third-party newsletter provider, ARARA, exposed the email addresses of 2.2 million newsletter subscribers.
  • The exposed data includes 92,300 records with additional information that SEGA and ARARA are still investigating, while SEGA says names, passwords, payment details, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and gender were not included.
  • ARARA said its email distribution service breach affected nearly 380 corporate clients and compromised 77 million email addresses.
  • ARARA stated that attackers used access to its service to send more than 7 million emails impersonating credit card companies in late October.
  • SEGA Fave's ALL.Net and Aime arcade network services remain offline after a separate unauthorized-access incident, which SEGA says is unrelated to the ARARA breach.

Products: all-net, aime, sega-lucky-kuji-online, sega-account

Vendors: arara, sega, sega-fave

York University breach exposed personal information dating to 2007 — Should Read

York University disclosed that an attacker accessed personal data submitted through departmental web forms between 2007 and 2026, potentially exposing sensitive information including contact details, government IDs, health data, and financial information. The university is notifying those whose government ID or financial data was affected and offering two years of identity-protection services.

  • York University discovered on October 25 that an unauthorized actor had accessed limited online forms used by university departments.
  • The incident affected forms submitted on 14 York University websites between 2007 and 2026.
  • The accessed information varied by person and included contact details, dates of birth, York ID numbers, government ID information, health information, academic and employment history, financial status, criminal background, demographic details, and images.
  • York University said the affected forms are now secure and will directly notify people whose government ID or financial account information was exposed, offering them two years of credit monitoring and identity theft protection.
  • The university has not disclosed how many people were affected or identified the perpetrators.

Data breach at hearing aid giant Amplifon impacts thousands — Should Read

Amplifon disclosed that a February cyberattack exposed U.S. customer data, including Social Security numbers, medical records, insurance details and financial information. While confirmed state filings cover tens of thousands, reports indicate the total may exceed 1.3 million people.

  • Amplifon discovered suspicious activity on February 11, and its investigation found that attackers had access to company files from January 18 through February 8.
  • The incident exposed customer information including names, Social Security numbers, driver’s licenses or state IDs, medical information, health insurance data, and financial information.
  • Amplifon reported that 85,804 people in Texas and 1,027 people in Vermont were affected, and it also filed a breach notice in California.
  • Several class-action law firms said 1,332,826 people may have been affected, but Amplifon did not confirm that total.
  • No hacking group had claimed responsibility for the incident as of Monday.

Vendors: amplifon

Verify the agent, secure the device: a closer look at governing AI end to end with Jamf and Okta — Optional

Okta and Jamf are expanding complementary AI governance controls: Okta governs agent identity, access, and runtime authorization, while Jamf manages the device, local AI tools, and browser/mobile usage. Together, the platforms aim to provide end-to-end visibility and enforcement from managed endpoints to the resources AI agents access.

  • Okta expanded Okta for AI Agents with endpoint discovery, Agent SSO, agent-to-agent connection controls, runtime enforcement through Agent Gateway, and planned kill-switch capabilities for active tokens and sessions.
  • Jamf AI Governance for Mac provides visibility, policy control, and audit reporting for supported AI tools including Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and OpenAI Codex.
  • Jamf announced planned browser controls to detect personal AI accounts and prevent actions such as corporate-file uploads, while mobile AI controls for iPhone and iPad are targeted for general availability in Q1 2027.
  • The article describes a combined model in which Jamf provides device-management and compliance context while Okta uses agent, user, and device information to make access decisions and log agent activity.
  • Jamf introduced platform capabilities including the Platform API Gateway, a Terraform provider, Routines automation, device-health assessment, and planned Ring Deployments.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, api-gateway, operating-system, browser, mobile-os

Products: okta-for-ai-agents, agent-gateway, agent-sso, shadow-ai-agent-discovery-for-endpoints, jamf-ai-governance, jamf-for-mac, claude-code, claude-desktop, openai-codex, jamf-platform-api-gateway, jamf-platform-terraform-provider, jamf-routines, jamf-ring-deployments

Vendors: okta, jamf, openai

Mitiga Named a Best Startup to Work For in Israel, 2026 — Optional

Mitiga was named one of Israel’s best startups to work for and one of five startups recognized by Dun & Bradstreet for AI adoption. The company says its AI-native transformation has accelerated detection engineering and product development while supporting its cloud and AI security platform.

  • Mitiga was named among Dun & Bradstreet’s 30 best startups to work for in Israel in its 2026 ranking of companies with up to 100 employees.
  • Mitiga was also one of five startups included in Dun & Bradstreet’s first list of startups leading in AI adoption and implementation.
  • Eighty percent of Mitiga’s team completed Dun & Bradstreet’s employee survey.
  • Mitiga says its R&D team’s multi-agent system increased detection output from 50 detections per month to more than 1,000, with people reviewing the results.
  • Mitiga reports that supporting a new data source was reduced from half a quarter to half a sprint.

Products: helios-aidr, mitiga-ai-agent-security

Vendors: mitiga, dun-bradstreet, loox, komodor, anthropic, hugging-face

Healthcare needs a coordinated response to industrialized cybercrime — Optional

Healthcare organizations face growing risk from industrialized cybercrime networks that sell specialized tools and services and increasingly use AI to identify vulnerabilities. The article argues that hospitals need a coordinated response to protect patient data, safety, and continuity of care.

  • Cybercrime is increasingly carried out by cooperating hacking and ransomware groups rather than individual actors.
  • Artificial intelligence is helping criminal groups find and pursue weaknesses they can exploit.
  • Underground markets let criminals purchase tools, infrastructure, and specialized services without developing them or possessing advanced technical expertise.
  • Healthcare organizations are increasingly targeted because they hold valuable data.
  • The article warns that industrialized cybercrime can threaten hospitals, patient safety, and uninterrupted essential services.

item.title: France Attributes IRGC Retail Attacks as SSHole Exploitation Spreads
item.content:encoded:
Window: 09 Nov 15:00 → 09 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers exploit SSHole OpenSSH flaw to breach Linux systems — Must Read

Attackers are actively exploiting the SSHole flaw (CVE-2026-123158) in OpenSSH on certain musl-based Linux systems to bypass password protections, steal credentials, and establish persistence. Administrators should upgrade to OpenSSH 10.6p2 or disable SSH password authentication and investigate suspicious logins, SSH keys, and TAC Agent artifacts.

  • Attackers are actively exploiting SSHole, tracked as CVE-2026-123158, to bypass authentication in OpenSSH on certain musl-based Linux systems such as Alpine Linux.
  • SSHole can allow login to accounts whose password field is set to an asterisk because an oversized password can cause musl’s password-hashing function to return the same value.
  • OpenSSH maintainers fixed the flaw in version 10.6p2 on November 5, and public exploit code became available about four hours later.
  • GreyNoise recorded successful attacks involving system and container reconnaissance, cloud metadata requests, attempts to obtain password hashes and root SSH keys, and changes to authorized_keys files for persistence.
  • Administrators are advised to update OpenSSH promptly or disable SSH password authentication and check for unexpected logins, unauthorized SSH keys, and TAC Agent files or startup services.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system

Products: openssh, tac-agent, musl-libc, alpine-linux

Vendors: openssh-project, musl, alpine-linux, greynoise, defused, previdian, watchtower

Hackers Exploit Qubole's Trusted AWS Access to Breach Customer Accounts and Steal Data — Must Read

Attackers used compromised Qubole AWS credentials to assume trusted customer IAM roles and steal secrets and S3 data from multiple AWS accounts between October 14 and 26. Organizations that have ever connected Qubole should review CloudTrail logs, revoke unused trust relationships, rotate exposed credentials, and restrict vendor role assumptions by source network and least privilege.

  • Attackers accessed multiple Qubole customers’ AWS accounts between October 14 and October 26 by using credentials for Qubole’s AWS account to assume customer roles that trusted it.
  • The attackers searched compromised environments for credentials in Lambda environment variables, AWS Secrets Manager, and SSM Parameter Store, then used TruffleHog to test stolen AWS, Entra ID, and Okta credentials.
  • The attackers also downloaded data from accessible Amazon S3 buckets, sometimes retrieving an entire bucket during one session.
  • Wiz advised organizations that have connected Qubole to AWS to review CloudTrail logs from October 1 onward for suspicious AssumeRole activity involving account 805246085872, attacker-linked IAM principals, IP addresses, or session names.
  • Wiz recommended removing unneeded Qubole roles, rotating secrets accessible to compromised roles, restricting role assumptions by source IP or VPC endpoint, and enabling S3 data events or server access logs for sensitive buckets.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam, secrets-manager, object-storage

Products: qubole, aws-iam, aws-cloudtrail, aws-lambda, aws-secrets-manager, aws-systems-manager-parameter-store, amazon-s3, trufflehog

Vendors: qubole, idera, amazon-web-services, wiz, sentra, trufflehog

France blames Iranian hackers for supermarket attacks that sparked fires — Should Read

France has attributed October cyberattacks on refrigeration controllers at roughly 700 retail locations, which caused major food losses and at least 15 fires, to the Iranian IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh unit. The campaign also targeted Schneider Electric equipment at small hydroelectric facilities.

  • France attributed October cyberattacks on refrigeration systems at French retail locations to Shahid Kaveh, a cyber-offensive unit linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
  • Attackers reportedly changed refrigeration-controller defrost settings to high temperatures overnight on October 11–12, disrupting food-preservation systems.
  • French authorities said approximately 700 retail locations were targeted, causing tens of millions of euros in food losses, significant material damage, and at least 15 fires.
  • The affected organizations included Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché, as well as smaller butcher shops, a slaughterhouse, and cooperative food-processing facilities.
  • Investigators also linked attacks against Schneider Electric equipment at small French hydroelectric installations to the same campaign, though those incidents had moderate effects.

Technologies: ics-scada

Products: fofa

Vendors: schneider-electric, fofa

Hackers Compromise Ethersphere's bee-js and Swarm Desktop to Deliver Wallet-Stealing Malware — Should Read

Attackers used stolen Ethersphere CI credentials to publish malicious bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases that stole Swarm wallet keys and passwords and installed cross-platform backdoors. Anyone who installed or ran either version should treat the system and wallet credentials as compromised, rotate secrets from a clean machine, and rebuild or thoroughly remediate affected hosts.

  • Attackers used stolen Ethersphere CI credentials to publish malicious bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases through the project’s own automated release workflows.
  • The malicious code stole Swarm Desktop’s encrypted wallet key file and the plain-text password stored alongside it, and it installed backdoors on Windows, macOS, and Linux systems.
  • bee-js 13.3.0 was available on npm for about 75 minutes, while Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 was available for about 8.5 hours before both malicious releases were withdrawn.
  • Ethersphere released Swarm Desktop 0.56.3 as a clean replacement, but updating or reinstalling does not remove any backdoor already installed or protect wallet keys already sent to attackers.
  • The malware contacted api.frameworkmetrics[.]xyz, installed an evjawbreaker remote shell on Linux and macOS, and installed a ScreenConnect remote-access client on Windows.

Technologies: ci-cd, package-registry, source-control, remote-access, antivirus

Products: bee-js, swarm-desktop, swarm-cli, bee-dashboard, github-actions, npm, screenconnect, microsoft-defender

Vendors: ethersphere, github, npm, connectwise, apple, microsoft

Russian cloud firm Beget rebuilds from scratch after data wiper attack — Should Read

Russian cloud provider Beget is rebuilding its infrastructure after an attacker accessed its management layer and deployed data-wiping scripts, destroying cloud, VPS, S3, Kubernetes, CDN, and configuration data. The company has restored part of its services but says much VPS data and backups cannot be recovered.

  • On November 1, an attacker accessed Beget’s management systems and deployed scripts that erased server data across its cloud infrastructure.
  • Beget said the incident destroyed data for its VPS, S3, and Kubernetes services, as well as CDN settings and IP configurations.
  • VPS binary backups were completely lost, while file backups survived only partially and may be available for about half of VPS users.
  • More than a week after the attack, Beget reported restoring 60% of shared hosting and 40% of the dedicated servers it manages.
  • Beget is manually checking roughly 1,000 servers for vulnerabilities and hidden scripts before bringing them back online.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, backup, container-platform, orchestration

Products: kubernetes

Vendors: beget, kubernetes

Vanderbilt cybersecurity incident impacting campus devices and systems — Should Read

Vanderbilt University is investigating and containing a cybersecurity incident that may affect campus devices and systems, advising students and staff to shut down devices and disconnect from university Wi‑Fi. The BYOD ransomware group has claimed responsibility and alleges it stole data.

  • Vanderbilt University announced that it is investigating and working to contain a cybersecurity incident that may affect campus devices and systems.
  • The university instructed students and employees to shut down their devices, disconnect from university Wi-Fi, and report suspicious activity to campus IT officials.
  • The ransomware group BYOD added Vanderbilt University to its leak site and claimed it had stolen data from the university.
  • BYOD has recently been linked to incidents involving Michigan State University and the University of New Mexico.
  • Halcyon reported a 40% increase in ransomware activity between July and September, with 111 groups claiming 2,766 attacks in 122 countries.

Binance denies data breach after alleged ShinyHunters claims — Should Read

Binance says it found no evidence that its systems or customer data were breached, dismissing a purported ShinyHunters listing claiming to sell data from 335 million users for $900,000 as likely a scam or infostealer-derived data.

  • A threat actor using the ShinyHunters name claimed to be selling records for 335 million Binance users for $900,000.
  • The claimed data allegedly included KYC documents, passwords, crypto wallet private keys, transaction histories, email addresses, phone numbers, and internal infrastructure information.
  • Binance said it found no evidence that its systems, customer KYC data, account credentials, wallet private keys, or internal infrastructure information were compromised in connection with the listing.
  • Binance said similar listings can involve data collected by infostealer malware from users’ own devices rather than data stolen from Binance systems.
  • Binance advised customers not to share passwords, two-factor authentication codes, seed phrases, or private keys and to remain alert to phishing attempts.

Vendors: binance

Ukraine arrests four in $5 million crypto scam targeting Germans — May Read

Ukrainian police arrested four suspects, including the alleged leader, over a fraudulent call-center network that reportedly stole more than €4.3 million from 135 German victims through fake cryptocurrency and stock investment schemes.

  • Ukrainian police arrested four suspects, including the alleged leader, over a network of fraudulent call centers that targeted people in Germany with fake cryptocurrency and stock investment platforms.
  • Investigators identified 135 German victims who collectively lost more than €4.3 million, and said scammers sometimes gained access to victims’ online banking accounts.
  • Ukrainian authorities searched more than 50 properties in Kyiv and other cities during raids in August and September, seizing devices, cryptocurrency wallets, documents, and more than $90,000 in cash.
  • Three suspects are being held before trial and a suspected co-organizer is under house arrest; those convicted could face up to 12 years in prison and property confiscation.
  • Ukraine has introduced legislation targeting scam call-center operations, while a separate anti-corruption investigation alleges officials accepted bribes to protect such centers from scrutiny.

The Biggest Threat to Your GRC Job Isn’t AI. It’s Ignoring AI. — Optional

Sponsored by Anecdotes, the article argues that GRC professionals should reskill for AI-driven operations by developing data literacy, governing agent performance, and maintaining auditable communication trails for agent actions.

  • The article says AI agents are already being used for GRC tasks such as control testing, evidence collection, and framework mapping.
  • It argues that GRC professionals should build data literacy so they can trace control evidence to its original source and assess whether data is trustworthy.
  • The article recommends treating AI agents like direct reports by setting measurable objectives, boundaries, accuracy standards, costs, and escalation rates.
  • It says organizations should ensure agent actions and handoffs are visible and time-stamped so humans can review and reverse them.
  • The article concludes that GRC managers who learn to direct and govern AI agents will be better positioned than those who continue only performing tasks that agents can automate.

Vendors: anecdotes, intsight

Pro-Russian hackers target European officials, offer rewards for personal information — Should Read

Pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) published personal data of senior European officials and offered cryptocurrency rewards for further information on them and their families, apparently in retaliation for a 2025 international law-enforcement disruption. Italy is investigating the campaign, while G7 foreign ministers are considering joint responses to pro-Russian cyber threats.

  • Pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) published personal information for 18 European politicians, law-enforcement officials, and journalists on a dedicated dark-web site.
  • The published profiles included phone numbers, email addresses, social-media accounts, and sometimes home addresses, and the group offered cryptocurrency rewards for further information about targets and their relatives.
  • Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said the campaign targeted him and his family to intimidate him over Italy's support for Ukraine.
  • The campaign appears linked to retaliation for a July 2025 multinational law-enforcement operation that took more than 100 NoName057(16) servers offline.
  • Italian prosecutors are investigating the publication of the personal information, and Tajani said G7 foreign ministers would discuss recent cyberattacks attributed to pro-Russian groups.

Default 'admin:admin' Server Password Helps Researchers Hack Two Automakers, Unlock and Start Cars — Should Read

Researchers found that two automakers' connected-car identity systems exposed an Apache Felix admin console with default admin:admin credentials, enabling takeover of customer accounts and remote vehicle unlock/start commands. The flaw was fixed shortly after disclosure, highlighting the risk of leaving development consoles and default passwords in production.

  • Researchers Shubham Shah and Sam Curry found that the login systems for two car brands exposed an Apache Felix administrator console using the documented default credentials admin:admin.
  • By exploiting differences in how the internet-facing edge and the Java server interpreted web addresses, the researchers reached the otherwise blocked administrator console.
  • Access to the identity servers allowed the researchers to change a target account’s email address and password, sign in through the normal app, and obtain the account’s access tokens.
  • Using those tokens, the researchers unlocked doors and started the engine only on cars they owned or had permission to test, and the affected United States systems were fixed about two hours after reporting.
  • A separate Australian attack used identity-server administrator credentials left in the app’s code for a test setup, and the researchers said the combined attacks could affect cars in Australia, the United States, and Canada.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam

Alleged AI-aided cyberattack exploits assistant interface to breach German web host — May Read

German hosting provider Mittwald said attackers exploited a flaw in its Model Context Protocol server to compromise 56 customer projects, remaining undetected for eight days. The company suspects the intruders used AI to accelerate their activity, though it provided no conclusive evidence beyond rapid actions in its logs.

  • Mittwald CM Service said attackers exploited a flaw in its Model Context Protocol server, which connects customer AI assistants to its mStudio website and hosting management platform.
  • The company reported that 56 customer projects were compromised and that the attacker remained undetected for eight days.
  • Mittwald managing director Robert Meyer said logs showed the attacker moving through systems unusually quickly, but the company provided no further evidence that AI tools were used.
  • Mittwald said external forensic experts are assisting the investigation, relevant authorities have been informed, and repeated scans had found no additional attacker activity as of Friday.

⚡ Weekly Recap: SSHole Exploited, APT Root RCE, Robot Takeovers, 15K Hacked Sites, and More — Optional

This weekly roundup highlights active exploitation of the SSHole OpenSSH flaw, supply-chain compromises of server-update mechanisms, and critical bugs affecting APT, Zyxel switches, and other widely deployed systems. The main takeaway is that unpatched internet-facing services, weak configurations, and compromised update channels remain high-impact entry points for attackers.

  • Attackers have attempted to exploit CVE-2026-123158, known as SSHole, which can allow sign-ins to passwordless accounts on Linux systems using OpenSSH with musl and PAM disabled, including Alpine Linux’s default configuration.
  • A flaw in Debian and Ubuntu’s APT package manager, CVE-2026-109518, can allow an attacker positioned between a host and package mirror to cause installation of an unverified package when HTTP sources and retry settings are used, with package scripts running with elevated privileges.
  • Zyxel patched CVE-2026-107441 in GS1900 network switches after attackers exploited it to compromise nearly 1,000 devices and steal configuration files and credentials.
  • Unknown attackers used compromised credentials to access OPSSHIELD’s update-distribution infrastructure and distribute a backdoor and data-stealing script through the cPGuard update channel.
  • The roundup also reports that roughly 15,579 websites are infected with malicious JavaScript used for credit-card skimming, ClickFix lures, iOS exploitation kits, and malicious redirects.
