item.title: LNbits Attacks and OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158 Drive Urgent Security Alerts
item.content:encoded:
Window: 09 Nov 07:00 → 09 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-123158) OpenSSH Password Authentication Bypass on musl Linux — Should Read

CVE-2026-123158 (“sshhole”) can let remote attackers bypass password authentication on vulnerable OpenSSH sshd instances built with musl and without PAM, especially Alpine Linux hosts. Patch to a fixed vendor package, restart sshd, and disable password authentication or restrict SSH access until remediation is confirmed.

  • CVE-2026-123158, also called “sshhole,” is an OpenSSH password-authentication bypass affecting sshd built with musl without PAM or with UsePAM disabled.
  • An attacker who can reach an affected SSH service can log in without knowing a password when password authentication is enabled, a target account’s /etc/shadow entry is exactly “*”, and another local account has a SHA-crypt hash.
  • Alpine Linux is the primary affected platform, while Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux are outside the affected glibc-and-PAM configuration.
  • OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes the flaw, and Alpine has backported patches for supported branches 3.16 through 3.24, though sshd must be restarted after updating.
  • Until patching is confirmed, the article recommends disabling password authentication on exposed musl-based hosts, auditing /etc/shadow for exactly “*” entries, and restricting TCP/22 access to trusted networks or a bastion host.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system, pam

Products: openssh, alpine-linux, musl-libc, cycognito-platform

Vendors: openssh, alpine-linux, musl-libc, cycognito

LNbits Urges All Operators to Shut Down Their Bitcoin Lightning Wallet Servers Amid Attacks — Should Read

LNbits urged all operators to immediately shut down their Bitcoin Lightning wallet servers after active exploits drained funds from at least one instance. Patches were expected within 24–48 hours, while the project’s hosted my.lnbits.com service was taken offline.

  • LNbits urged all operators of its open-source Bitcoin Lightning wallet servers to shut them down amid a wave of attacks while it prepares security fixes.
  • An operator reported that attackers used an exploit to withdraw 2,285,545 satoshis, about 0.023 Bitcoin, from his server before it was shut down.
  • LNbits initially told operators to disable its Paywall add-on, then issued a broader shutdown notice about 80 minutes later.
  • LNbits took its hosted my.lnbits.com instances offline and said services would return within 24 hours, while a developer estimated patches would be available within 24 to 48 hours.
  • The project had not publicly identified the exact add-on used in the reported incident or said how many servers were affected as of 09:00 UTC.

Products: lnbits, paywall, my-lnbits-com

Vendors: lnbits

Taiwan-Based Hacker Used BOSSAI AI Agents to Steal Taipei Emergency Dispatch Records — Should Read

Acronis researchers say a Taiwan-based attacker used locally run, safety-stripped AI agents to steal Taipei emergency dispatch records and target poorly secured systems in Taiwan, Mexico, and Thailand. The case shows AI can scale reconnaissance and exploitation, but the compromises largely relied on exposed APIs, default credentials, SQL injection flaws, and unpatched systems.

  • Acronis researchers said a single attacker based in Hualien City, Taiwan, used a setup called BOSSAI with AI agents to target hundreds of organizations in at least 11 countries.
  • The agents extracted emergency dispatch case records for seven Taipei districts from a public-facing 119 emergency-services API, including incident times, response types, case status, and street-level locations.
  • The agents found a Taipei fire department platform that exposed patient data from 2018, including ECG readings and ambulance video footage, without requiring a login.
  • Commercial AI models generally refused direct requests to conduct attacks, so the attacker used locally run safety-stripped versions of DeepSeek, GLM, and Qwen for most attack activity.
  • The confirmed compromises largely involved weak protections, including exposed data, default root credentials, SQL injection points, and unpatched Oracle databases.

Technologies: database

Products: bossai, grok, claude-code, codex, cursor, deepseek, glm, qwen, oracle-database

Vendors: acronis, xai, anthropic, openai, cursor, deepseek, zhipu-ai, alibaba-cloud, oracle

Former OpenAI Engineer Pleads Not Guilty to Planting Covert Device in Executive Meeting Room — May Read

Former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan pleaded not guilty to allegedly planting an encrypted covert recording device in an executive conference room to capture sensitive conversations. Prosecutors say he is a flight risk and faces up to five years in prison if convicted.

  • Former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan pleaded not guilty in San Francisco federal court to a charge of intercepting oral communications.
  • Prosecutors allege that Alfozan placed a sophisticated recording device in an OpenAI executive conference room to record sensitive conversations.
  • A grand jury indicted Alfozan late last month on one count of interception of oral communications.
  • Alfozan has been held without bail since his October 9, 2026 arrest, and his next hearing is scheduled for November 17, 2026.
  • If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison, a $250,000 fine, and three years of supervised release.
